scenarios.name: Normal sinus rhythm
scenarios.changes: Default parameter set.
scenarios.limitations: Idealised geometry; PA interval longer than reference; deep S in V2–V3; amplitudes depend on scalar torso factors.
scenarios.validation: tests/physiology/normalSinus.test.ts (intervals vs reference ranges, lead identities, activation order).

scenarios.name: Sinus bradycardia
scenarios.changes: Vagal tone 0.5 → 0.9.
scenarios.limitations: Autonomic coefficients are nominal.

scenarios.name: Sinus tachycardia
scenarios.changes: Vagal 0.5 → 0.1; sympathetic 0.1 → 0.6.
scenarios.limitations: No β-adrenergic effect on ventricular APD; APD adapts within one beat (no slow memory).

scenarios.name: Sinus arrest with junctional escape
scenarios.changes: Sinus arrest on (live at the current time so the pause is visible).
scenarios.limitations: All-or-none arrest; no gradual sinus slowing or pause distribution.

scenarios.name: SA exit block (type II, 4:3)
scenarios.changes: SA exit block every 4th discharge; junctional escape rate lowered to 30 /min so the pause is not interrupted.
scenarios.limitations: Deterministic pattern; type I (Wenckebach) SA exit block not modelled; SA depolarisation itself is ECG-silent (as in reality).

scenarios.name: First-degree AV block
scenarios.changes: Minimum AV nodal conduction time 65 → 180 ms.
scenarios.limitations: Lumped AV node.

scenarios.name: Second-degree AV block, Mobitz I (Wenckebach)
scenarios.changes: AV-nodal ERP 300 → 650 ms (H-to-A recovery), recovery amplitude 180 → 300 ms, τ 90 → 200 ms; junctional escape 30 /min.
scenarios.limitations: Nodal parameters are nominal (chosen to show the mechanism at a resting sinus rate).

scenarios.name: Second-degree AV block, Mobitz II (3:2)
scenarios.changes: Infra-Hisian block of every 3rd impulse.
scenarios.limitations: Deterministic pattern (real Mobitz II is intermittent); usually accompanied by bundle-branch disease, which is not combined here.

scenarios.name: 2:1 AV block
scenarios.changes: Infra-Hisian block every 2nd impulse.
scenarios.limitations: Nodal 2:1 block (by ERP) also emerges at fast atrial rates but is not used here.

scenarios.name: Complete AV block (nodal) – junctional escape
scenarios.changes: Complete AV nodal block on.
scenarios.limitations: Escape rate fixed (no rate response).
scenarios.validation: Automated test: "complete AV block, junctional escape" (tests/physiology/scenarios.test.ts).

scenarios.name: Complete infra-Hisian block – ventricular escape
scenarios.changes: Complete infra-Hisian block on.
scenarios.limitations: Single fixed escape site.
scenarios.validation: Automated test: "complete infra-Hisian block, ventricular escape" (tests/physiology/scenarios.test.ts).

scenarios.name: Premature atrial complex (non-compensatory pause)
scenarios.changes: Ectopic focus low RA, single, coupling 520 ms, every 4 beats.
scenarios.limitations: SA-node reset is all-or-none; sinus-node entrance delay not modelled.

scenarios.name: Premature ventricular complex (compensatory pause)
scenarios.changes: Ectopic focus LV lateral, single, coupling 450 ms, every 3 beats; retrograde AV conduction 'concealed' (default).
scenarios.limitations: Detector-measured QRS duration of the ectopic beat can overestimate the true value when the T wave starts immediately (model truth is shown alongside).

scenarios.name: Ventricular bigeminy
scenarios.changes: Ectopy pattern bigeminy, coupling 450 ms.
scenarios.limitations: Fixed coupling (no re-entry or triggered mechanism underlies the coupling).

scenarios.name: Ventricular trigeminy
scenarios.changes: Ectopy pattern trigeminy, coupling 450 ms.
scenarios.limitations: Fixed coupling.

scenarios.name: Ventricular couplet
scenarios.changes: Ectopy pattern couplet, coupling 420 ms, every 4 beats.
scenarios.limitations: Fixed coupling.

scenarios.name: Interpolated PVC (no pause)
scenarios.changes: Ectopy single, coupling 330 ms, every 3 beats.
scenarios.limitations: Whether interpolation occurs depends on nominal nodal parameters.

scenarios.name: Focal atrial tachycardia
scenarios.changes: Ectopy focus LA, rate 150 /min.
scenarios.limitations: Automaticity is imposed (rate parameter), not generated by ionic currents; no warm-up/cool-down.

scenarios.name: AV nodal re-entrant tachycardia (typical)
scenarios.changes: Dual pathway on; retrograde conduction 'conducted', retrograde nodal time 20 ms, retrograde ERP 150 ms, slow-pathway minimum AH 210 ms; PAC from the low RA, coupling 330 ms (one PAC). Calibrated to typical AVNRT: CL 317 ± 43 ms, HA 45.8 ± 7.7 ms (Katritsis et al. 2015).
scenarios.limitations: Pathways are lumped links joined at the His bundle (no lower common pathway, no atrial tissue in the circuit apart from the inputs). Rate depends on nominal pathway parameters.

scenarios.name: Orthodromic AVRT (concealed accessory pathway)
scenarios.changes: Accessory pathway left lateral, antegrade off; AV-nodal ERP 300 → 130 ms; PAC from the high RA, coupling 330 ms.
scenarios.limitations: Pathway parameters nominal; the shortened nodal ERP is required for this geometry's short circuit.

scenarios.name: Antidromic AVRT
scenarios.changes: Manifest left lateral pathway (antegrade ERP 250 ms); retrograde AV conduction 'conducted' with ERP 120 ms; PAC from the high RA, coupling 300 ms.
scenarios.limitations: Pathway parameters nominal.

scenarios.name: Ventricular pre-excitation (manifest pathway)
scenarios.changes: Accessory pathway left lateral, antegrade on.
scenarios.limitations: Pathway conduction time and refractoriness are nominal; the degree of pre-excitation depends on the (fast) AV-nodal conduction of this model. Delta-wave onset is detected from the rise of the spatial ECG magnitude.

scenarios.name: Typical atrial flutter (macro-re-entry around the tricuspid annulus)
scenarios.changes: Flutter anatomy on (CTI CV × 0.2, CTI APD × 1.3); burst of 6 stimuli at 230 ms from the low RA after every 3rd sinus beat until re-entry starts.
scenarios.limitations: Spherical idealised atria: the circuit is shorter than in a real RA, so a slow isthmus (CV × 0.2, nominal) is needed to obtain a cycle length of ≈ 180 ms (≈ 330/min, near the upper part of the usual human range). Flutter-wave morphology on the surface ECG is not validated (no saw-tooth calibration).

scenarios.name: Atrial fibrillation (PV-triggered, remodelled atria)
scenarios.changes: PV focus 450/min (CL 133 ms); atrial APD map heterogeneity SD 40 %, atrial CV 0.45 m/s, atrial reference APD 300 ms (calibrated, see limitations); AV-nodal concealment 0.25; sympathetic tone 0.3.
scenarios.limitations: Event-driven graph without source–sink or curvature effects, so wavelet dynamics are qualitative. The atrial reference APD (300 ms at CL 1000) was chosen so the emergent RA cycle length (≈ 170–240 ms) lies near reported human AF cycle lengths (e.g. coronary-sinus AFCL 171 ± 27 ms, Verma et al. 2008); the APD rate map below CL 400 ms is extrapolated. Concealment and heterogeneity magnitudes are nominal. f-wave morphology is not validated.

scenarios.name: Monomorphic VT (focal / automatic mechanism)
scenarios.changes: Ectopy focus RVOT, 170 /min.
scenarios.limitations: Not re-entrant VT; the triggering mechanism (e.g. cAMP-mediated triggered activity) is not modelled.

scenarios.name: Scar-related re-entrant VT (monomorphic)
scenarios.changes: Scar substrate on (isthmus CV × 0.18, border-zone CV × 0.12, isthmus APD × 1.3) with the refractory floor raised to 0.60 of reference APD; burst of 8 stimuli at 260 ms from the scar border after every 3rd sinus beat until re-entry starts.
scenarios.limitations: The cycle length is governed by the refractory floor as much as by the circuit, because this engine's re-entry has no excitable gap (see docs/SCIENTIFIC_LIMITATIONS.md); the floor is therefore raised for this scenario, which suppresses physiological APD shortening at short diastolic intervals. The scar geometry is an idealised sphere with one straight isthmus, not patient anatomy, and all three substrate factors are nominal. The slow border zone also distorts the baseline tracing: in sinus rhythm before induction this substrate gives QRS ≈ 112 ms and QT ≈ 560 ms, wider and longer than an uncomplicated post-infarct ECG. Entrainment, the response to pacing manoeuvres, and the relation between isthmus length and cycle length are not validated.

scenarios.name: Polymorphic VT
scenarios.changes: Scar substrate with isthmus CV × 0.12 and border-zone CV × 0.25, refractory floor 0.60; same burst as the monomorphic scenario.
scenarios.limitations: Reduced-order: the wave break arises from the imposed geometry and refractoriness, not from source–sink mismatch or wavefront curvature, which this engine does not represent. The model does not draw a sharp line between polymorphic VT and fibrillation — the two scenarios here differ in degree of organisation and rate, not in kind. Nor is this rhythm's changing axis distinguishable from the twisting of the torsades scenario by rotation alone (net/total rotation 0.94 here against 0.89 there); what differs is the setting and that this rhythm is sustained rather than self-terminating. Cycle length depends on the refractory floor as described for the monomorphic scenario. Baseline tracing in sinus rhythm shows QRS ≈ 132 ms and QT ≈ 506 ms.

scenarios.name: Torsades de pointes
scenarios.changes: Ventricular APD × 1.3 and the transmural and apicobasal gradients × 2.6 (long QT with increased dispersion of repolarisation — the measured torsades substrate, Kozhevnikov et al. 2002), and the M-cell island × 3, the enlarged zone of long refractoriness of the LQT2 wedge. Torsades generator on: 16-site ring, source advancing 0.6 of a step per beat, re-excitation 10 ms after local recovery, paired loop at 45 ms, runs of up to 34 beats every 10th sinus beat, first beat at 390 ms. Two restitution parameters are changed for the run and are NOMINAL, tuned so that the simulated tracing meets the measured torsades criteria rather than derived from data: the APD floor 0.45 → 0.5 (the period of the circulating source) and the depth of CV restitution 0.5 → 0.85, which at the ~10 ms diastolic intervals of the run slows conduction to about 39 % of normal. Conduction does slow steeply near the point of block, but this value is not calibrated. The ERP/APD ratio is left at its default 0.92 — unlike v1.3–v1.5, nothing is tuned to obtain capture.
scenarios.limitations: Partial. The source is imposed, not emergent: the ring stands in for a drifting rotor, which this engine cannot grow. v1.6.0 re-examined that directly rather than assuming it. The M-cell island the mapping studies name as the obstacle was added to the model, and capture was then scanned over coupling interval, island size and amplitude, electrotonic smoothing and conduction velocity. Capture turned out to be all-or-nothing — 0 % of the ventricle at a 415 ms coupling interval, 100 % at 435 ms — with no interval in between that leaves a surviving line of block. The reason was measured: the recovery front sweeps the ventricle in about 140 ms (96 % of it refractory at 374 ms, none at 514 ms) whereas a premature wave needs 250–280 ms to cross it, so whatever is refractory when the beat starts has recovered before the wavefront reaches it. Functional re-entry needs an obstacle that persists for a whole lap, and in a real heart that obstacle is the rotor core held open by wavefront curvature — source–sink physics this event-driven graph does not represent. Only anatomical obstacles work here, which is why flutter and scar VT are validated and this is not. Consequences: the run does not arise from the long QT — the same generator on a normal-QT substrate still runs — so this scenario cannot be used to predict torsade risk, only to show what the mechanism looks like on the surface ECG. Two further routes were tried and failed, and are recorded with the numbers in SCIENTIFIC_LIMITATIONS.md: two competing fixed foci gave a continuous tracing at 231 /min but only a 177° two-state axis flip rather than a progressive twist, and a source that always moved to the globally best-recovered site locked into a two-site ping-pong. Of the measured criteria, one still falls outside its target: the complexes carry 3.3 local extrema each against the 1–3 of a smooth recording, so they remain slightly more fragmented than a real tracing. Spindle length (one node per run of 16 beats), rate, continuity, envelope and axis sweep are now all within range.

scenarios.name: Ventricular fibrillation
scenarios.changes: Ventricular repolarisation dispersion SD 0.20 and refractory floor 0.79 of reference APD (calibrated — see limitations); burst of 14 stimuli at 240 ms from the RV apex after every 3rd sinus beat.
scenarios.limitations: The cycle length is a CALIBRATION, not a prediction. Because re-entry in this engine has no excitable gap, its period is simply the refractory period: measured across 18 runs, cycle length was 0.408–0.422 × reference APD against a predicted 0.414. With the default floor the model fibrillates at ≈ 150 ms, far faster than human VF, so the floor was raised to 0.79 to bring the local activation interval to 220 ms — against measured human VF of 218 ± 24 ms in vivo (Nair et al. 2012) and a dominant frequency of 4.5–6.4 Hz (Bradley et al. 2011). That calibration suppresses physiological APD shortening at short diastolic intervals. Wavelet dynamics are qualitative: there is no source–sink mismatch, wavefront curvature or rotor meander, phase singularities are not computed, and the fibrillatory waveform's amplitude and spectrum are not validated. The dispersion map is a smoothed random field, not patient anatomy, and its magnitude is nominal; it also lengthens the baseline QT (≈ 420 ms in sinus rhythm before induction).

scenarios.name: Right bundle branch block
scenarios.changes: RBB block on.
scenarios.limitations: The idealised RV geometry/mass produces an implausible frontal QRS axis in RBBB, so the morphology is only partly reproduced.

scenarios.name: Left bundle branch block
scenarios.changes: LBB block on.
scenarios.limitations: Retrograde entry into the LV Purkinje network is limited by a nominal retrograde junction delay (40 ms), calibrated so that QRS reaches the ≥ 140 ms LBBB criterion (Strauss et al. 2011); precordial morphology is affected by the near-field V2–V4 artefact.

scenarios.name: IKr inhibition 50 % (long-QT pattern)
scenarios.changes: gKr × 0.5 in TP06; tissue: ventricular APD and gradients × 1.085, longitudinal CV × 1.
scenarios.limitations: Partial: ionic currents act in single cells only; tissue sees scaled APD/CV. No EADs/torsades; the M-cell layer is not represented in tissue, so transmural dispersion is under-represented. The TP06 → tissue mapping under-predicts the QT effect of hERG block about threefold: dofetilide at a dose giving ≈ 51 % block prolonged QTc by 79 ms in man (see the clinically calibrated dofetilide scenario), whereas this mapping gives ≈ +25 ms.

scenarios.name: IKr inhibition 90 %
scenarios.changes: gKr × 0.1 in TP06; tissue: ventricular APD and gradients × 1.173, longitudinal CV × 1.
scenarios.limitations: Partial: ionic currents act in single cells only; tissue sees scaled APD/CV. As above; TP06 produced no EADs under these conditions, so torsades cannot arise.

scenarios.name: IKr gain of function (short-QT pattern)
scenarios.changes: gKr × 2 in TP06; tissue: ventricular APD and gradients × 0.872, longitudinal CV × 1.
scenarios.limitations: Partial: ionic currents act in single cells only; tissue sees scaled APD/CV. SQTS1 alters IKr inactivation kinetics, not just conductance.

scenarios.name: Hyperkalaemia (K⁺ 7.0 mmol/L)
scenarios.changes: Extracellular K⁺ 5.4 → 7.0 mmol/L. TP06: ventricular APD × 0.982, conduction × 0.802, AP amplitude × 0.901. Calibrated shape: phase-3 width × 0.54.
scenarios.limitations: Partial. The direction of every change comes from the TP06 cell model, but TP06 mapped onto the tissue changes the T wave very little (taller by ≈ 20 % at 8 mM, no U wave at 3 mM), so the T/U morphology is calibrated rather than emergent. In real patients T-wave features correlate weakly with serum K⁺ (r ≤ 0.2 in routine ECGs; hyperkalaemic changes in only ≈ 46 % at 6–9.3 mmol/L), so the tracing shows the textbook pattern, not a predicted dose–response. 5.4 mmol/L is TP06's reference value, at the upper end of the normal serum range. Sinus-node and AV-nodal effects are not modelled; ST depression in hypokalaemia is not reproduced.

scenarios.name: Hyperkalaemia, advanced (K⁺ 8.5 mmol/L)
scenarios.changes: Extracellular K⁺ 5.4 → 8.5 mmol/L. TP06: ventricular APD × 0.965, conduction × 0.596, AP amplitude × 0.834. Calibrated shape: phase-3 width × 0.33.
scenarios.limitations: Partial. scenarios.name: Hypokalaemia (K⁺ 3.0 mmol/L)
scenarios.changes: Extracellular K⁺ 5.4 → 3.0 mmol/L. TP06: ventricular APD × 1.044, conduction × 1.112, AP amplitude × 1.168. Calibrated shape: phase-3 width × 2.52, slow terminal component 45 % delayed by 30 % of the APD.
scenarios.limitations: Partial. The direction of every change comes from the TP06 cell model, but TP06 mapped onto the tissue changes the T wave very little (taller by ≈ 20 % at 8 mM, no U wave at 3 mM), so the T/U morphology is calibrated rather than emergent. scenarios.name: Sodium-channel blockade (INa −50 %)
scenarios.changes: gNa × 0.5 in TP06; tissue: ventricular APD and gradients × 1.004, longitudinal CV × 0.785.
scenarios.limitations: Partial: ionic currents act in single cells only; tissue sees scaled APD/CV. Use-dependence (rate-dependent block) is not modelled; atrial/His–Purkinje effects not mapped.

scenarios.name: L-type Ca²⁺-channel blockade (ICaL −50 %)
scenarios.changes: gCaL × 0.5 in TP06; tissue: ventricular APD and gradients × 0.771, longitudinal CV × 1.011.
scenarios.limitations: Partial: ionic currents act in single cells only; tissue sees scaled APD/CV. The dominant clinical effect (AV-nodal slowing) is not modelled because the AV node is a lumped link without ionic currents.

scenarios.name: Hypercalcaemia (serum Ca²⁺ 3.2 mmol/L)
scenarios.changes: Serum total calcium 2.4 → 3.2 mmol/L; ventricular APD shifted by -24 ms (30.1 ms per mmol/L, Young et al. 2021).
scenarios.limitations: The slope is linear and was measured in populations whose calcium lies in or near the reference range (Mendelian randomisation, UK Biobank, n = 76 226: 3.01 ms per 0.1 mmol/L, 95% CI 2.03–3.99). Applying it at 3.2 mmol/L is extrapolation, and the true change is probably larger: the equivalent slope measured against *ionised* calcium in haemodialysis patients is about threefold steeper (8.55 ms per 0.1 mmol/L). T-wave shape changes and the tall peaked T of severe hypercalcaemia are not reproduced, because the tissue action-potential shape is fixed. No arrhythmia arises from calcium alone in this model.

scenarios.name: Hypocalcaemia (serum Ca²⁺ 1.6 mmol/L)
scenarios.changes: Serum total calcium 2.4 → 1.6 mmol/L; ventricular APD shifted by +24 ms (30.1 ms per mmol/L, Young et al. 2021).
scenarios.limitations: The slope is linear and was measured in populations whose calcium lies in or near the reference range (Mendelian randomisation, UK Biobank, n = 76 226: 3.01 ms per 0.1 mmol/L, 95% CI 2.03–3.99). Applying it at 1.6 mmol/L is extrapolation, and the true change is probably larger: the equivalent slope measured against *ionised* calcium in haemodialysis patients is about threefold steeper (8.55 ms per 0.1 mmol/L). T-wave shape changes and the tall peaked T of severe hypercalcaemia are not reproduced, because the tissue action-potential shape is fixed. No arrhythmia arises from calcium alone in this model.

scenarios.name: EAD / DAD triggered activity
scenarios.changes: Long-QT tissue substrate (ventricular APD × 1.17, the mapped effect of 90 % IKr block) plus triggered beats every 2nd sinus beat at a coupling interval of 390 ms — the EAD takeoff time measured in the cell (τ_f × 0.5, ICaL × 2.5, IKs × 0.2 at CL 1000 ms).
scenarios.limitations: Partial by construction. The afterdepolarisations themselves exist only in the single-cell model — the tissue receives their *timing* as an ectopic stimulus, it does not generate them, because the ionic model is not coupled cell-to-cell. Neither does the surface ECG show the afterdepolarisation itself. In addition, TP06 does not produce EADs from IKr block alone at any degree of block; the published modification used here shortens the ICaL f-gate time constant to enlarge the window current (Vandersickel et al. 2014), and DADs require an added RyR leak (Chakraborty et al.). Those are modifications of the cell model, not emergent properties of it.

scenarios.name: Dofetilide — clinical dose
scenarios.changes: 500 µg single dose (peak plasma 2.7 ng/mL). Tissue, calibrated to the human study: ventricular APD +61.6 ms, phase-3 width × 1.59.
scenarios.limitations: Partial: the size of the effect is calibrated to one randomised study in 22 healthy volunteers (Johannesen et al. 2014) at a single dose, not predicted. TP06 alone (51 % hERG block at the free Cmax) would lengthen the APD by only ≈ 8 % (the gKr × 0.5 mapping gives × 1.085). The torsade risk category (high) is clinical knowledge, not a model output. Use-dependence, state-dependent binding and heart-rate effects are not modelled.

scenarios.name: Quinidine — clinical dose
scenarios.changes: 400 mg quinidine sulfate single dose (peak plasma 1.8 µg/mL). Tissue, calibrated to the human study: ventricular APD +61.2 ms, phase-3 width × 1.7.
scenarios.limitations: Partial: the size of the effect is calibrated to one randomised study in 22 healthy volunteers (Johannesen et al. 2014) at a single dose, not predicted. TP06 alone predicts APD × 1.134 at the free Cmax. The torsade risk category (high) is clinical knowledge, not a model output. Use-dependence, state-dependent binding and heart-rate effects are not modelled.

scenarios.name: Flecainide 4× free Cmax
scenarios.changes: IKr × 0.19, ICaL × 1.00, INa × 0.69 in TP06; tissue APD × 1.155, ventricular CV × 0.885.
scenarios.limitations: Partial: block is treated as a fixed reduction in conductance. Use-dependence (rate-dependent block, prominent for flecainide), state-dependent binding, trapping and metabolite activity are not modelled, and TP06 has no late sodium current. The torsade risk category shown (intermediate) is clinical knowledge, not a model output: this model cannot predict whether a given drug causes torsades, only how the measured channel block changes repolarisation and conduction. Arrhythmia does not arise spontaneously from the drug in this model; combine it with the triggered-activity or polymorphic-VT scenarios to see the consequence.

scenarios.name: Verapamil — clinical dose
scenarios.changes: 120 mg single dose (peak plasma 130 ng/mL). Tissue, calibrated to the human study: ventricular APD +0.1 ms, phase-3 width × 1.092, AV-nodal conduction time +32 ms.
scenarios.limitations: Partial: the size of the effect is calibrated to one randomised study in 22 healthy volunteers (Johannesen et al. 2014) at a single dose, not predicted. TP06 alone predicts marked APD shortening (× 0.73 at 4× the free Cmax) from L-type Ca²⁺ block; in man QTc did not change significantly, while PR lengthened by 32 ms through AV-nodal Ca²⁺-channel block. The torsade risk category (low) is clinical knowledge, not a model output. Use-dependence, state-dependent binding and heart-rate effects are not modelled.

scenarios.name: Acute ischaemia — Proximal LAD
scenarios.changes: Culprit Proximal LAD; grade 2 (APD × 0.895 and AP amplitude × 0.655 at the centre of the territory, soft border zone). Raise the grade to 3 in Parameters to add slow conduction in the zone (QRS distortion, tombstoning).
scenarios.limitations: Partial. Territories are the standard AHA vessel assignment on an idealised heart, not individual coronary anatomy. The size of the ST shift is calibrated to 1-minute balloon occlusion in man (LAD median 0.26 mV, Haeberlin et al. 2014); established STEMI is often larger. TP06 has no ATP-sensitive K⁺ current, hence the calibrated amplitude loss. This scenario is the acute phase; the hyperacute, evolving, subacute and old phases are separate scenarios in this group, and the phase can be changed for any culprit in Parameters. There is no reperfusion and no clock — a phase is a state you select, not a process. The model's precordial R-wave progression is poor (SCIENTIFIC_LIMITATIONS.md), which affects the baseline QRS but not the direction of the ST changes.

scenarios.name: Infarct, hyperacute — Proximal LAD
scenarios.changes: Culprit Proximal LAD, grade 2, phase "hyperacute". The phase sets three weights: how much injury current remains (ST), the necrotic fraction of the wall (Q) and the extra peri-infarct APD (T). Change the phase in Parameters to step through the whole sequence.
scenarios.limitations: Partial. The phase is a state you select, not a process: the model has no clock for healing and the weights are nominal interpolations of the described sequence. Q waves do not appear in V2–V3, where an anterior infarct should show them most clearly, because those leads are dominated by a deep S in this model's poor R-wave progression — there is no R for the infarct to remove. The peri-infarct APD boost needed to invert the T at all also stretches QT to about 490 ms in the subacute phase, longer than a typical healing infarct. No reperfusion, no ventricular aneurysm (persistent ST elevation) and no subendocardial (non-Q-wave) infarction as a separate entity. See SCIENTIFIC_LIMITATIONS.md ("Infarct phases").
